newsitem.title: USA: NY Court turns down NYC plan to sell water system.
newsitem.headline: NY Court turns down NYC plan to sell water system.

text.p: The New York State Court of Appeals on Thursday, upholding previous court decisions, ruled that New York City could not go ahead with a plan to sell its water and sewer system by issuing $2.3 billion of bonds.

Asked if the Giuliani Administration likely would drop its plans to try to sell the system, which the city has owned for 150 years, a spokesman for the the Water Finance Authority Board replied: "I assume so."
He added "The court made some pretty strong statements here."

A spokesman for New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani was not immediately available to comment. Giuliani had taken his fight to sell the water system to court, suing the New York City Comptroller, Alan Hevesi, who had said he would block the deal by declining to approve the bond offering.

In prepared remarks, the city comptroller's office said: "Comptroller Alan Hevesi has been a long-standing critic of using the sale of a precious asset to pay non-water system operating costs and fill budget gaps."

Under Giuliani's plan, the sale would have given the city about $1 billion for capital projects that were not related to its water system, the court ruling explained. Around $1.3 billion of the new bonds would have been used to retire the financing for improvements to the city's system, which provides about eight million residents of New York City and Westchester County with 1.5 billion gallons of water a day.

The state's highest court held that "Use of the Authority's debt power is permissable only if the purchase of the water system on the terms proposed is of a 'water project' or furthers 'other corporate purposes' of the Authority," according to the decision written by Chief Judge Judith Kaye.

Rejecting the city's contention that the municipal bond sales should be allowed unless "patently illegal," the court, in a unanimous decision, found that the legislation that created the Water Finance Authority did not permit the transaction. "Like the courts below, we conclude that the statute does not permit the proposed transaction and it therefore cannot be consummated."
